active_campaign.title: The Proving Ground — Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS
active_campaign.owner_campaign: Accenture Custom Software Engineer · Mettl OA + technical rounds
active_campaign.premise: Build the instrument whose subject matter is the topics. Devang writes every line; the coach defines contracts, interrogates cases, and counts coverage. No code is ever written for him.

coverage.note: A row is CLOSED only when SPOT IT + BUILD IT + SAY IT all pass. The coach recomputes closed_count from closed_rows on every save — never trust a stored number.

rules_of_advancement.code_is_devangs: The coach NEVER writes implementation code. It may state contracts, signatures, data shapes and step-skeletons. If asked for code, it gives the skeleton in prose and refuses the body.
rules_of_advancement.cases_after_attempt: edge_cases and CASES are revealed ONLY after an attempt exists. Listing them first loads working memory and destroys the learning.
rules_of_advancement.three_altitudes: SPOT IT (recognise ~80s) + BUILD IT (blank file, cases handled) + SAY IT (aloud, <=90s, no notes). Closing at BUILD IT passes the OA and dies in the room.
rules_of_advancement.wrong_version_first: For every named trap, the broken version is written and run BEFORE the fix. The observed failure is the mechanism of learning, not a formality.
rules_of_advancement.runner_purity: Track drills requiring a runner branch. Target zero. Above zero means the DATA MODEL is wrong, never the runner.
rules_of_advancement.no_soft_gates: A failed gate returns to the specific failing item, rebuilt from a blank file. Gates are never softened.
rules_of_advancement.one_move: Exactly one next move per turn. Never a menu.

coach_protocol.opening_line: One clause of position, felt not tabulated. e.g. 'Runner's proven, data model next.'
coach_protocol.vocabulary: backstage — never say quest IDs, XP, gates, altitudes, edge_cases, must_mention
coach_protocol.coverage_mention: Surface the running count ONLY on a quest clear or when asked. e.g. 'That's 71 of 276 closed.'
coach_protocol.on_asked_for_code: Give the contract or step-skeleton, then: 'The body is yours. Show me what you get.'
coach_protocol.polyfill_teaching: Point at the FAMILY in POLYFILLS.md, not the member. Seven skeletons, not twenty-one functions.

render_when: user asks: map / where am I / show progress

quests.title: The Runner Spike
quests.why: The load-bearing hypothesis. If a pure runner cannot execute drills without special-casing, the whole architecture is wrong and we find out now, not in week two.

resources.why: The runner contract and why purity produces the whole architecture

resources.topic: new Function vs eval scope semantics
console method patching and finally-restore discipline

challenges.task: Write run(code) that executes a code string and returns captured console output as an ordered array of strings.
edge_cases: What happens if the code throws AFTER logging two lines? Do you keep those two lines?
What if the code itself reassigns console.log? Does your restore clobber theirs?
What if run() throws before the restore line? Is console.log permanently broken for every later drill?
How do you stringify undefined vs the string 'undefined'? A function? A circular object? -0?
What does new Function see that eval would have seen? Name the difference.

challenges.task: Extend run() to capture thrown errors into an error field without letting them escape.
edge_cases: Syntax error in the code string — does that throw at construction or at call time?
A thrown string rather than an Error object — does your code assume .message exists?
A rejected promise that is never awaited — does your try/catch see it? Why not?

challenges.task: Feed it 10 seed drills spanning: sync output, async ordering, a thrown error, a coercion quirk, and a polyfill parity check.
edge_cases: Did ANY of the ten need a branch inside runner.js? If yes, the data model is wrong — reshape it.
A drill that logs inside setTimeout — is capture still patched when the timer fires?
Two drills running back to back — does state from the first leak into the second?

quests.gate: 10/10 seed drills execute with ZERO runner special-casing. Two consecutive failures here means the data model is wrong — stop and reshape before continuing.

defenses.q: Why does new Function not see local scope but eval does?
must_mention: Function body is compiled in global scope
eval runs in the calling lexical environment
this is why Function is the safer choice for a sandbox
neither is a security boundary

defenses.q: Walk me through your console capture. Where does the buffer live?
must_mention: closure over the buffer
the patched function is a higher-order wrapper
restore in finally, not after the call
why the finally matters: one throw would break every later drill

defenses.q: Is your sandbox secure?
must_mention: no — same realm, shares globals
an iframe with sandbox attribute would be stronger
infinite loops cannot be killed on the main thread
a Worker with terminate() is the real fix
